💡 Our offer: we document the condition of each item of equipment in the handover report for your home in Kenitra or Sale — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from the start to handover.

141.title: An old bathroom is renovated in order, not at random — a step in the wrong place costs you redoing the work. 🚿
141.body:
The correct order: first diagnosis and demolition; second, the new networks — plumbing and electrical before any wall is closed; third, waterproofing — on a clean, dry support, with a 24-hour water test; fourth, tiling; fifth, sanitary fittings; and finally the touch-ups. Whoever tiles before waterproofing redoes everything, and whoever fits the equipment before tiling damages it with their own hands.

💡 Our offer: we renovate your old bathroom in Rabat or Kenitra in the correct order — a clear written study, and photo follow-up stage by stage, so you do not redo a single step.

142.title: You live in the home and want to renovate it? Renovating while living there is an art that is possible — if it is well organised. 🏠
142.body:
The secret is gradual progress: room by room, an area protected from dust, and a bathroom and kitchen that keep working for as long as possible. And a written programme that tells you each day what will happen, so life does not stop — it just changes a little.

💡 Our offer: we renovate your apartment in Rabat or Sale while you live in it — a written programme room by room, dust protection, and photo follow-up at each stage on WhatsApp.

143.title: The slope of the terrace is formed in the concrete, not afterwards.
143.body:
Does your terrace in Rabat collect water after every winter? The problem is not the waterproofing — it is the slope. 💧

According to DTU 43.1, the slope is made in the structural work so water flows by itself towards the drainage — if you wait until the end, you will add layers and fix the mistake at the cost of the mistake.

💡 Our offer: before starting terrace waterproofing in Rabat, we check its slope and explain what needs to be fixed — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from the start to handover.

144.title: According to DTU 43.1, the terrace must have dual drainage — a main outlet + a backup outlet (trop-plein).
144.body:
Did you know the terrace must have a second outlet for water if the first one gets blocked? This is the rule that saves your home. 🌧️

If the first outlet gets blocked with leaves or dust, the water exits through the second and does not rise above the wall. A terrace without a second outlet is a terrace waiting for a flood.

💡 Our offer: we check your terrace drainage in Kenitra and add the backup outlet if it is missing — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from the start to handover.

145.title: Waterproofing does not stick to dust and damp.
145.body:
Do you want terrace waterproofing in Temara that lasts? Before the waterproofing is laid, the surface must be clean and dry — that is the rule. 🧹

The surface must be thoroughly cleaned and completely dry before work begins — otherwise the waterproofing will peel off from the start. The craftsman who starts without cleaning the surface is building on sand.

💡 Our offer: before any terrace waterproofing in Temara, we prepare the surface well — cleaning, drying, and inspection — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from the start to handover.

146.title: When redoing waterproofing, the upstands (les relevés) are rebuilt from scratch on the wall — at least 10 cm according to DTU 20.12 — because that is the point where water gets in.
146.body:
Redoing the waterproofing of an old terrace in Sale? The new waterproofing is not complete unless the upstands are rebuilt from scratch. 🛠️

New waterproofing over old, worn upstands is incomplete waterproofing from the start.

💡 Our offer: for redoing the waterproofing of your terrace in Sale, we rebuild the upstands from scratch and check every sensitive point — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

147.title: Water that stays standing after rain is telling you that the slope does not carry the water to the drain — and that weakens the waterproofing over time.
147.body:
After the rain, does water stay standing on your terrace? That is not an ordinary puddle — it is a message from your terrace. 💧

According to DTU 43.1, the slope is formed in the concrete so the water flows on its own: if you see a puddle that remains, you should have it inspected before the problem grows.

💡 Our offer: we inspect your terrace in Rabat after the rain and pinpoint where the water stands — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

148.title: NM 10.8.913 is the Moroccan waterproofing standard cited in specifications in Morocco — and DTU 43.1 is the corresponding French reference.
148.body:
Does your quote include a reference for the waterproofing? If it does not mention NM 10.8.913, ask about it — that is the Moroccan waterproofing standard. 📋

A waterproofing quote that cites the reference makes clear what will be carried out, while a quote with no reference at all leaves everything open to interpretation.

💡 Our offer: for any terrace waterproofing in Kenitra, our quote cites the reference, the materials and the stages — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

149.title: Waterproofing requires a dry surface and suitable weather — in summer and autumn the surface dries well and the materials bond properly.
149.body:
Do you want terrace waterproofing in Temara? The best time is before winter — not in the middle of it. ☀️

If you start waterproofing in the middle of winter, moisture makes the work incomplete from the start, and you will redo it later at your own expense.

💡 Our offer: if you want terrace waterproofing in Temara, send us a message now and we will schedule the work at the right time — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

150.title: A well-waterproofed terrace is a complete system — four rules: the slope in the concrete so water flows (DTU 43.1), double drainage with a backup outlet, upstands of at least 10 cm (DTU 20.12), and a 24-hour water test before covering.
150.body:
Is your terrace leaking? The problem is not in a single layer — it is in the whole system. 🏗️

If just one is missing, the whole system weakens.

📸 The photos:

A — The slope: the water flows on its own towards the drain.

B — Double drainage: the main one and the backup.

C — The upstands: at least 10 cm.

D — The water test: the proof before covering.

💡 Our offer: we inspect your terrace system in Rabat — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

151.title: Does your roof leak every winter? The problem is 4 steps that were not done properly. 💧
151.body:
Roof waterproofing is built on 4 rules: a slope in the concrete so water runs off, double drainage so water finds its way, raising the waterproofing up the edges by at least 10 cm, and a 24-hour water test before handover. One missing step, and the whole roof is at risk.

📸 The photos:

A — The slope: water runs towards the drain.

B — Double drainage: drain + overflow for emergencies.

C — Raising the waterproofing up the edge: at least 10 cm.

D — The water test before handover.

💡 Our offer: we inspect your roof and repair the waterproofing according to these four rules — a clear written study, and photo follow-up stage by stage.

152.title: Do you want to waterproof your roof? The first step is not the product — the first step is the roof itself: clean and dry. 🧹
152.body:
Waterproofing does not stick to dust or to moisture: a dirty or wet surface makes the layer peel off after a few months, even if the product is good. Full cleaning and drying before application is not a detail — it is the foundation of everything.

💡 Our offer: before any waterproofing, we clean the surface and make sure it is completely dry — a clear written study, and photo follow-up stage by stage.

153.title: One blocked drain = a roof drowned in water. The solution? A second path for the water. 🌧️
153.body:
If the single drain gets blocked with leaves and dirt, the water stays on the roof and looks for its way — most often inside the house. Double drainage (drain + overflow) gives the water a second outlet if the first gets blocked: the roof does not stay drowned, and the house stays protected.

💡 Our offer: we review your roof drainage and add a second outlet if one is missing — a clear written study, and photo follow-up stage by stage.

154.title: Water that stays standing on the roof finds its way inside — the slope is what stops it. 💧
154.body:
The slope of the roof is not made with the waterproofing — it is made in the concrete itself, before the waterproofing. If the slab is completely flat, water stands in puddles and presses on the waterproofing until it leaks. A correct roof lets water run towards the drain from the first drop of rain.

💡 Our offer: we inspect your roof's slope and fix its drainage at the root — a clear written study, and photo follow-up stage by stage.

155.title: After the rain, do you find puddles of water standing on your roof? That is not normal — it is a message from your roof. 💧
155.body:
Puddles that remain standing mean the slope does not carry the water to the drain: with sun and time, the waterproofing wears out in exactly those places, and the leak starts there. A correct roof dries completely after rain, with no puddles.

💡 Our offer: we inspect your roof after the rain and pinpoint where the water stands — a clear written study, and photo follow-up stage by stage.

156.title: If your roof drain gets blocked in the middle of a storm, where will the water go? The answer: the overflow. 🛟
156.body:
The overflow is a second outlet placed slightly higher than the drain: if the water rises above the limit, it exits through the overflow before entering the house. Without an overflow, the roof turns into a pond — and with a little time, the water finds its way through the ceiling.

💡 Our offer: we make sure your roof has a working overflow, and we add one if it is missing — a clear written study, and photo follow-up stage by stage.

157.title: The waterproofing was done well, and then someone came and walked on it in site boots? That is where the leak begins. 👷
157.body:
The waterproofing layer stays sensitive until it is covered: walking on it with heavy tools, storing materials on it, and piercing it carelessly — all of these wound it without showing. Protecting the waterproofing during the work is not a luxury, it is part of the work itself.

💡 Our offer: we protect your waterproofing during the work and monitor every stage — a clear written study, and photo follow-up stage by stage.

158.title: The first winter rains? That is the best moment to see whether your waterproofing is working or not. 🔍
158.body:
After the first heavy rain, go up to the roof and look: is the water running towards the drain? Are there standing puddles? And inside, is there a trace of damp in the ceiling? Inspection after the first rain reveals the problem while it is small — before it grows and becomes expensive.

💡 Our offer: we inspect your roof after the first rain and repair what needs repairing — a clear written study, and photo follow-up stage by stage.

159.title: Does your terrace keep water standing on it after rain? The problem is not the waterproofing — it is the slopes. 💧
159.body:
If you are looking for terrace waterproofing in Casablanca, know this rule: the terrace slopes are formed in the concrete, before the waterproofing is laid — that is the DTU 43.1 rule. Water must go to the drain without collecting. A terrace with no slopes, even with good waterproofing, keeps water standing, and it looks for the weakest point to get in.

💡 Our offer: before waterproofing your terrace, we inspect the slopes and fix them before the waterproofing — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

160.title: Your terrace downpipe got blocked with a leaf or dirt — will the water stay standing over your head? No, if you have a second outlet. 🌧️
160.body:
If you are looking for terrace waterproofing in Kenitra, know this rule: DTU 43.1 requires double drainage — two outlets for the water, or a downpipe plus an overflow. If one gets blocked, the second works. A terrace with a single outlet is a terrace waiting for the first blockage to flood.

💡 Our offer: we inspect your terrace water outlets and add the second outlet if it is missing — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

161.title: Did you know you can measure waterproofing quality with a ruler? The waterproofing that rises up the wall must be at least 10 cm. 📏
161.body:
If you are looking for terrace waterproofing in Marrakech, know this rule: DTU 20.12 requires the waterproofing to rise at least 10 cm above the terrace, on the roof wall. Less than that, and water gets in from the side. Measure with your own eyes before you pay.

📸 The photos:

A — The waterproofing rising up the roof wall.

B — Measuring with the ruler: at least 10 cm.

C — The angle and the junction between the wall and the terrace.

D — The waterproofing protected and completed.

💡 Our offer: we inspect your terrace waterproofing with you, ruler in hand, and fix it if it falls short — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

162.title: Waterproofing does not stick to dust or to a wet surface — it sticks to a clean, dry surface. 🧹
162.body:
If you are looking for terrace waterproofing in Agadir, know this rule: before waterproofing, the surface must be cleaned of dust and dirt, and be completely dry. Waterproofing laid on a wet surface peels off later, and the problem shows after the first rain. Cleaning and drying are not a waste of time — they are half the job.

💡 Our offer: preparing your surface before waterproofing — cleaning, drying and inspection — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

163.title: How do you know the waterproofing is good before covering it with protection? With water — 24 hours of testing. 💧
163.body:
If you are looking for terrace waterproofing in Temara, know this rule: we fill the terrace with water, leave it for 24 hours, and monitor from below. If no leak appears, only then do we cover the waterproofing with protection. Whoever covers without testing buries the problem — and whoever tests gives you the proof before you pay.

💡 Our offer: a 24-hour water test before we cover your waterproofing — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

164.title: The terrace is not a single layer — it is an order: the slopes, the waterproofing, and the protection. If you reverse the order, you will redo the work. 🏗️
164.body:
If you are looking for terrace renovation in Casablanca, know this rule: first the slopes so water flows, then the waterproofing according to the Moroccan standard NM 10.8.913, then the protection that shields the waterproofing from the sun and from foot traffic. Each layer has its role — and the layer that comes before protects the one after it.

💡 Our offer: we build your terrace layer by layer, in the correct order — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

165.title: Traditional plaster or plasterboard? The answer is not in fashion — it is in the room. ✨
165.body:
If you are looking for living-room renovation in Rabat, know this rule: traditional Moroccan plaster is the signature of beauty — for living rooms, dry rooms and decoration. Plasterboard is speed and precision — for straight ceilings and short deadlines. And wet rooms have another choice. In both cases, the quality of the substrate and the structure determines the ceiling's lifespan.

💡 Our offer: we help you choose the right plaster for each room in your home — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

166.title: A successful slab does not start with the truck — it starts before it, and finishes after it. 🏗️
166.body:
If you are looking to build a villa in Kenitra, know this rule: before pouring, we check the steel and the formwork according to the design office's plans. During pouring, correct vibration without adding water to the mix. And after pouring, curing with water and removing the formwork at the right time. A slab prepared this way lasts — and one poured haphazardly, you pay for later.

💡 Our offer: pouring your slabs with checks before, during and after — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

167.title: You prepared your complete bid, and you arrived one minute late? In public tenders, being late eliminates you before the envelope is even opened. ⏰
167.body:
If you are looking for public tenders in Rabat, know this rule: the bid must be submitted within the deadline set in the notice, in the required form — no incomplete envelope, no late submission. Whoever prepares their bid at the last minute is gambling on luck — and whoever prepares it early enters the competition calmly.

💡 Our offer: we support you in studying public tender files — a full reading of the file before you calculate the price — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

168.title: Something unexpected happened on site? Act now — but write everything down immediately afterwards. ✍️
168.body:
If you are looking for additional work in Marrakech, know this rule: additional work requires a written order from the project owner. And in a real emergency, we carry out the work to protect the site, then confirm in writing immediately — with photos and measurements. Whoever works on a verbal basis risks never being paid.

💡 Our offer: every change on your site is documented in writing and with photos before it is carried out — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

169.title: Did you know the right product comes with its paperwork? The certificate and the marking are the proof before it is installed. 📄
169.body:
If you are looking to build a villa in Kenitra, know this rule: every material that arrives on site must have a certificate of conformity and clear marking — cement, steel, and waterproofing. We compare the paperwork with the goods before unloading. A material with no paperwork does not enter the site.

📸 The photos:

A — The certificates and documents on the site table.

B — The marking on the product.

C — The delivery note against the goods.

💡 Our offer: we check your site materials with you — by certificates and marking — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up.

170.title: Before the concrete truck arrives, who checked the reinforcement? Steel that isn't checked gets covered in concrete — and the mistake stays inside. 🏗️
170.body:
If you're looking to build a villa in Tangier, know this rule: before pouring, we compare the reinforcement against the design office plans — diameter, number, and spacing. Checking before pouring is cheap; correcting after pouring is expensive.

💡 Our offer: we check your slab reinforcement with you before pouring — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

171.title: Paint peeling after a few months? The problem isn't the colour — it's the primer coat that was never applied. 🎨
171.body:
If you're looking for villa painting in Fes, know this rule: before the colour, you need the primer coat — it seals the pores of the wall and lets the paint adhere properly. Skipping this coat to save money means repainting everything later.

💡 Our offer: painting your villa from primer to final colour — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

172.title: Your villa's boundary wall is leaning, or cracking from the bottom? A boundary wall isn't just a wall — it's a structure like the house, and it needs foundations. 🧱
172.body:
If you're looking to build a villa boundary wall in Casablanca, know this rule: a wall without foundations leans over time, and the crack shows from the bottom. A proper wall is built on foundations, in stone and concrete, with joints that let it breathe — not just bricks on the ground. One built properly protects the house for years; one built in a hurry becomes a danger to anyone passing by.

💡 Our offer: building and renovating your villa boundary wall on the right foundations — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

173.title: You closed the wall over the pipes and cables without photographing them? Later, if you want to drill for a screw, you'll be playing the lottery. 📸
173.body:
If you're looking for bathroom renovation in Temara, know this rule: before closing up, we photograph the entire network — water, electricity, and drainage — and give you the photos with the plan. This is the house's memory: years later, you'll know exactly where every pipe runs.

💡 Our offer: photographic documentation of your home's networks before closing — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

174.title: A small measuring error repeats on every floor and in every room — and in the end, it becomes a big error. 📏
174.body:
If you're looking to build a villa in Agadir, know this rule: the quantities in the quote must be checked against the plans and against reality on site — before starting, and at every stage. A small difference not caught at the start grows with every repetition — and correcting it at the end is expensive.

💡 Our offer: we review your project's quantities with you before starting — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

175.title: Do you maintain your terrace once a year, or leave it until it starts leaking? Waterproofing doesn't survive without inspection. 🔍
175.body:
If you're looking for terrace waterproofing in Casablanca, know this rule: once a year, the terrace needs a full visit — water outlets clear, waterproofing upstands on the wall sound, and corners protected. A small problem is easy to fix today; left alone, it grows until it becomes a leak.

A — Inspecting the water outlets.

B — Cleaning the terrace before winter.

C — Checking the waterproofing on the wall.

D — Checking after the first winter.

💡 Our offer: annual visit for your terrace — inspection of outlets, waterproofing and corners — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up.

176.title: Is your bathroom leaking into the neighbours below? The problem isn't the tiling — it's the waterproofing that must be done before the tiling. 🚿
176.body:
If you're looking for bathroom renovation in Marrakech, know this rule: before the tiling is laid, the bathroom needs complete waterproofing — the floor and the shower walls. Tiling is not a waterproofing layer; it's only a decorative finish over the waterproofing. Laying tiles without waterproofing hides the problem — and the water comes out underneath.

💡 Our offer: waterproofing your bathroom before the tiling — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

177.title: The steel bars sticking out of the slab waiting for the next floor — have you left them to rust? Steel that rusts today weakens tomorrow's building. 🔩
177.body:
If you're looking to build a villa in Kenitra, know this rule: protruding starter bars (les aciers en attente) must be protected from water and air until building resumes — covered and preserved. Steel that rusts loses its strength; steel that is protected stays ready for the next stage.

💡 Our offer: protecting your project's steel before we continue building — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

178.title: Does your front door close properly? Does cold, dust and noise get through? A door isn't just wood — it's the house's first barrier. 🚪
178.body:
If you're looking for villa renovation in Casablanca, know this rule: the front door must be fitted to measure, with no gaps, strong hinges and a good lock. A badly fitted door lets cold in during winter and noise in every day — a well-fitted door protects the house and raises its value.

💡 Our offer: a made-to-measure front door — precise fitting and high-end finishes — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

179.title: A site where rubble and dirt are everywhere — is that the company's image? A clean site is a safe site. 🧹
179.body:
If you're looking for villa renovation in Temara, know this rule: rubble must be gathered in its place, materials must be stored tidily, and walkways must stay clear. An organised site protects workers, protects materials, and lets the work move fast — a dirty site hides mistakes and causes accidents.

💡 Our offer: an organised, clean site from start to delivery — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

180.title: A pipe is leaking, and you can't find a way to reach it? The problem isn't the pipe — it's that it was sealed in the wall with no maintenance access. 🔧
180.body:
If you're looking for villa renovation in Agadir, know this rule: pipes and cables running inside the wall must be placed in a technical duct (gaine) with a maintenance hatch — so that if a problem occurs, we can repair it without breaking the wall. Sealing everything in with no access point makes you pay twice: once for building, once for breaking open.

💡 Our offer: technical ducts with maintenance hatches in your project — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

181.title: A stone wall gives a house an authentic character — but only if it's built properly. 🪨
181.body:
If you're looking to build a villa in Marrakech, know this rule: exposed stone must be built stone by stone, with the right mortar and regular joints — not just decoration on top of a wall. A wall built properly lasts for generations; a wall built in a hurry cracks and crumbles.

💡 Our offer: stone walls using the traditional method — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

182.title: Does your tiling sound hollow under your feet? The problem isn't the tiling — it's the floor beneath it. 🟫
182.body:
If you're looking for villa renovation in Kenitra, know this rule: before tiling, the screed (la chape) must be level, dry and sound. Tiles laid on a sloped or hollow screed sound hollow and crack over time. A level screed is half the tiling job.

💡 Our offer: preparing your screed before tiling — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

183.title: You submitted your file for a public tender, and your price wasn't even opened? The problem isn't the price — it's a missing document. 📋
183.body:
If you're looking into public tenders in Kenitra, know this rule: most files are rejected for administrative reasons, not technical ones — an incomplete file never gets its price opened. Before calculating the price, read the full specifications, gather the required documents, and make sure the bid bond matches the required form and amount. Only a complete file reaches the pricing stage.

💡 Our offer: if you're a contractor looking for a works partner, we work with you with clear files and well-organised documents — a written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

184.title: Are your house foundations chosen from a catalogue? No — the ground chooses. 🏗️
184.body:
If you're looking to build a villa in Casablanca, know this rule: the type of foundations is decided by the nature of the ground and the load of the building, after a geotechnical study. The wrong foundations are paid for dearly: differential settlement and cracks in the walls. The right foundations cost less than repairing the house afterwards.

💡 Our offer: before building, we examine the ground and build the foundations that suit it — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

185.title: Your basement is taking in water, and you painted the wall? Paint won't stop anything — treat the source. 💧
185.body:
If you're looking for basement damp treatment in Casablanca, know this rule: water comes from three directions — rising from the ground, seeping in from the side, or condensation — and each cause has its treatment: watertight internal tanking, drainage that relieves pressure, and sensitive points first.

💡 Our offer: basement diagnosis before repair + treating the source — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up.

186.title: Found an offer much cheaper than the rest? Ask yourself: where will they make up the difference? 💸
186.body:
If you're looking for villa renovation in Marrakech, know this rule: a price below the real cost doesn't become profitable later — the difference shows up on site: cheaper materials, incomplete work, or extra works that weren't in the calculation. Slashing prices to win the contract just shifts the problem to cash flow, quality, or a dispute. Better to lose a contract than win a loss-making site.

💡 Our offer: our quote is detailed and clear — each item states what it includes, with no surprises — send us a WhatsApp message and we'll explain everything before you start.

187.title: A terrace above a bedroom? Here, waterproofing has no room for error — not a single drop is allowed. 💧
187.body:
If you're looking for terrace waterproofing in Casablanca, know this rule: if there's a lived-in room under the terrace, the waterproofing must be complete — slopes so water drains away, per DTU 43.1, waterproofing per Moroccan standard NM 10.8.913, and protection that shields it from sun and foot traffic. A terrace over a garage is not a terrace over your bedroom — here, every layer must be right.

💡 Our offer: we examine your terrace above lived-in rooms and repair it layer by layer — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

188.title: Your terrace is leaking? Before you sign for the repair, ask these 3 questions — the answers will show you whether the contractor knows what he's doing. 🔍
188.body:
If you're looking for terrace leak repair in Kenitra, ask: first — are the slopes correct, and does the water flow to the drain? Per DTU 43.1, slopes are formed in the concrete. Second — does the waterproofing rise at least 10 cm up the wall? Per DTU 20.12. Third — will you do a 24-hour water test before covering up? If he has no clear answer to all three, don't sign with him.

💡 Our offer: diagnosis of your leak using the three questions + a clear written study — send us a WhatsApp message and let's start.

189.title: Tiling on a waterproofed terrace isn't just decoration — it's the protection you walk on every day. 🏗️
189.body:
If you're looking for terrace tiling in Tangier, know this rule: a terrace is built layer by layer — slopes so water drains away, waterproofing per Moroccan standard NM 10.8.913, then protection that shields the waterproofing from sun and foot traffic. Tiling laid with no protection, stuck directly onto the waterproofing, exposes it to damage over time. Protection isn't optional — it's what makes the waterproofing last.

💡 Our offer: we build your terrace layer by layer, in the right order — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.

190.title: Rain has fallen, the roof is wet — should we waterproof now or wait? Wait. 💧
190.body:
If you're looking for terrace waterproofing in Rabat in winter, know this rule: waterproofing doesn't stick to a wet surface — it sticks to a clean, dry surface. Waterproofing applied to a wet surface peels off later, and the problem shows after the first winter. In winter, drying time isn't wasted time — it's half the job. Rushing in winter means redoing the work in spring.

💡 Our offer: preparing your surface before waterproofing — cleaning, drying and inspection — a clear written study, and transparent follow-up from start to handover.
